title: The few onward recipients the returns do name
question: Each agency must list its five highest-paid contractors. Who are they, and are any privately owned?
finding: Each return names five payees: the agency's highest-paid contractors. For Children's Council they are child-care providers. In 2024, when it paid 238 contractors more than $100,000 each, the five were Wu Yee Children's Services ($3.3 million); Kai Ming Inc ($2.6 million); Cross Cultural Family Center ($2.6 million); Mission Neighborhood Centers Inc ($2.2 million); Holy Family Day Homes Of San Francisco ($1.9 million); its 2025 return names none and counts no contractor above $100,000. Across both agencies and five years, 5 private companies or corporations with no tax-exempt record found are among the named providers ($7.4 million), led by Bright Horizons with $4.6 million in 2021, 2022, 2023, 2025. 11 more top-five places went to home-based or individual providers ($3.1 million); they are not named here.
how: Form 990 asks for the five highest-paid independent contractors and for the number of contractors paid more than $100,000. Those lists were read for Children's Council and Wu Yee Children's Services for tax years ending June 2021 to June 2025, using the latest version of each return. A payee is named here when its name matches the licensee or name of a licensed child-care centre or a City-paid nonprofit, or when it is plainly a firm; people, individual licensees and providers that may be private homes are added together. Licensed places and City network sites are the payee's own.
limits: Five names a year are a sliver of the payments: the count of contractors above $100,000 shows how many more there are, and smaller providers are not counted at all. The amount is everything the agency paid the provider that year, from State and City money together. Families choose the provider. A return that names no contractors may reflect a change in how the agency classified provider payments rather than a change in who was paid. Matching is by name. Wu Yee's lists also hold builders, a caterer and a cleaning firm, which are ordinary costs of running its own centres.
